output.title: West Apron Barrier Scope Discrepancy
output.shortSummary: The owner requested eight west apron barriers as additional scope, while RFI-118 states the same eight are included under tender detail C-21. The superintendent marked positions but reported zero barriers in the current takeoff and an unavailable tender drawing. Concrete placement is on hold pending reconciliation.
output.responsiblePartyHypothesis: Responsibility remains unresolved: the owner describes added scope, but the architect identifies an existing tender requirement. The discrepancy could reflect owner-added work or a contractor takeoff omission; C-21 and the agreed scope must be checked.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Please install eight concrete barriers along the west apron. These are additional to our current package. I have asked the field crew to start setting out tomorrow. Submit the additional scope for review.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Owner direction identifies the quantity and location and characterizes the work as additional.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Eight west apron barriers are already included in the tender scope, detail C-21. The owner email refers to the same eight locations, not eight further units. Proceed to C-21; we do not consider this additional work.
evidenceReferences.explanation: The architect disputes added scope and links the same eight locations to tender detail C-21, which is not supplied.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Marked eight west apron positions after reading the email and RFI-118. The tender drawing referenced in the response was not available on site; our current takeoff has zero barriers here. PM asked us not to place concrete until the discrepancy is reconciled.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Confirms receipt of both communications, performed layout, and the placement hold. It does not establish that layout was outside scope.

missingEvidence: Tender detail C-21 and the agreed scope documents establishing whether these eight barriers were included.
Reconciliation of the current takeoff with the tender drawing.
Clarified owner and architect direction resolving the contradictory scope descriptions.
output.recommendedNextStep: Ask the superintendent to obtain C-21, reconcile the eight marked locations against the agreed scope and takeoff, and obtain clarified direction through the PM before concrete placement.

output.title: North-loop trench scope reconciliation

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Crew called the last 80 feet of north-loop trench extra during toolbox talk because it was beyond yesterday’s stakes. Today we completed that 80 feet and used the scheduled excavator. No route or depth changed.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Documents the performed work and crew’s characterization, while confirming unchanged route and depth; it does not establish added scope.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Original issued C-08 includes 480 linear feet of north-loop trench, including the final 80 feet from station N4 to N5. Tender revision unchanged.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Places the final N4–N5 segment within the original tender scope.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: The 400 feet previously installed plus today’s 80 feet equals the original 480-foot scope. No additional alignment, quantity or method has been instructed. N4-N5 was missed in the crew’s daily stakeout, not the contract.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Reconciles installed quantities to the baseline and attributes the perceived extra work to omitted daily stakeout.

output.recommendedNextStep: Reconcile the superintendent’s production record with C-08 and RFI-009 and record the final 80 feet as original-scope completion.

output.title: Unshown Water Main at T3
output.shortSummary: An active water main exposed at T3 conflicts with the original utilities survey and prevents planned dry excavation. Excavation stopped and the pipe was protected. The utility engineer confirmed the discrepancy and directed trench security pending a crossing support design.
output.responsiblePartyHypothesis: The records suggest an unshown existing utility and a contract survey discrepancy rather than contractor installation error. Responsibility for resulting protection, standby and any crossing support remains subject to review.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: At T3, 1.4 m below grade, exposed an active 150 mm water main crossing the pump feeder route. Stopped excavation and protected the pipe. Utility locator witnessed the crossing. Planned dry excavation cannot proceed safely.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Documents the encountered main, excavation stoppage and pipe protection; the recording time is the observed event-time proxy.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Original contract survey U-11 and bore logs for T3 show no utility crossing to 2 m depth. Survey envelope includes the exposed location.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Establishes that the contract survey covered the location and indicated no crossing at the encountered depth.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Confirmed in the field: active water main at T3 is absent from the contract utilities survey U-11. Keep the trench secure while we design a crossing support detail. No contractor installation error caused this conflict; track protection and standby records for project review.
evidenceReferences.explanation: Independently confirms the discrepancy, directs trench security and identifies support design as pending; contractor receipt is not documented.

missingEvidence: Contract provisions allocating existing utility and survey risks.
Confirmation of when the contractor received the RFI response.
Issued crossing support detail and records establishing the extent of protection, standby and subsequent work.
output.recommendedNextStep: Ask the superintendent to confirm receipt of the RFI direction, document protection and standby activity, and obtain the crossing support detail for comparison with the original scope.
